Hi Alice — great write-up, and thanks for the SOC2 doc. I sketched a practical MAP that aligns evaluation gates to procurement tranches and included an acceptance matrix so procurement knows what to expect before each tranche is billed. Summary below; I'll attach the MAP workbook (MAP-v3.xlsx) with timelines and owner columns.

High-level approach (pilot -> tranche1 -> tranche2):
- Pilot (Sept start, 2–4 week eval): 2-node private cluster (H100-preferred small pool) or equivalent Dedicated slice (4 A100 equiv) to validate latency, throughput, and correctness on 20k daily active users simulation. Acceptance: 95% of requests < 120ms p95, 99th < 350ms, and model output recall within the eval prompt-set threshold.
- Tranche 1 (Q4 early): Expand to a 16–32 A100-equivalent pool (or 8–16 H100-equivalent depending on availability). Purpose: scale-throughput baseline for production traffic + start canary rollout on 10% of requests. Accept when throughput target met and cost per 1k tokens within 15% of forecast.
- Tranche 2 (Q4 late / Q1 next yr): Full capacity to target peak load with autoscaling headroom and cross-region redundancy. Acceptance: SLA hit rates, failover test, and load-run stability for 72 hours.

Procurement lead-time guidance (current market signal):
- H100 (newer SKU): lead time 12–18 weeks for dedicated supplier reservations; spotty immediate availability for private on-prem SKUs depending on vendor channel.
- A100 (mature SKU): 8–12 weeks for reservations; more predictable stock through cloud partners for Dedicated pools.
- For private/on-prem air-gapped installs, add 4–6 weeks for logistics, KMS/HSM onboarding, and SOC2 evidence review.

Canary/onboarding acceptance matrix (condensed):
- Security: SOC2 checklist items validated (pen test not required for pilot)
- Performance: p95 and p99 latency targets, throughput RPS target
- Cost: unit economics per 1k tokens within threshold
- Reliability: KV cache hit rate > 40% during the run and graceful fallback to smaller model variant on OOMs

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I'll draft the MAP workbook and propose concrete dates tied to your procurement windows; Marissa will own the reservation contract language and payment cadence.
2) Karthik, can you produce two sizing sheets (A100-based and H100-based) with expected throughput curves and an estimated monthly committed spend for each tranche?
3) Alice/Tom — confirm whether the private deployment route requires HSM integration (if yes, we should add 4 weeks in lead times).

I attached MAP-v3.xlsx (contains the dates and owner columns). If that looks good, we can lock the pilot window and have Marissa issue a reservation statement for Tranche 1 conditional on acceptance.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
